title: Finite fibres of a semiabelian generic graph projection
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $P,Q\to S$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. The group laws, identity sections and inverse maps are morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $S$, $K=\kappa(\eta)$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and $P_\eta,Q_\eta$ for the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Given a $K$-group homomorphism $u:P_\eta\to Q_\eta$, let $\Gamma\subseteq P\times_SQ$ be the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of $P_\eta\xrightarrow{(1,u)}(P\times_SQ)_\eta\to P\times_SQ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\pi:\Gamma\to P$ be the first projection. Then for every point $x\in P$, the fibre $\Gamma_x=\Gamma\times_P\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ has a finite underlying set of points. No reducedness assertion about this fibre is included.

source.place: G. Faltings, Finiteness Theorems for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields, in Arithmetic Geometry (1986), Chapter II, section 2, Lemma 1 proof, printed pp.10-11: the two assertions about the projection of the graph closure. Local copy WANTED; online primary-source proof read at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~lefourns/contenu/Zywina/Faltings.pdf .

proof.text: Every algebraically closed geometric fibre of $P$ is integral, hence nonempty and connected, by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$. The algebraically closed extension criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] therefore makes every residue-field fibre geometrically connected. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to $P\to S$: the identity section makes $P$ nonempty, and $S$ is integral and normal as required. In particular $P_\eta$ is integral. Denote its generic point by $\xi$.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth; the geometric-integrality and connectedness inputs are the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: Put $Y=P\times_SQ$ and let $a:P_\eta\to Y$ be the prescribed graph map. Both $Y$ and its closed subscheme $\Gamma$ are locally Noetherian. Indeed over a Noetherian affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, product affine charts have algebras $B\otimes_A C$ with $B,C$ finitely presented over $A$; the union of their finite generating sets generates the tensor algebra, and passing to a closed subscheme takes a quotient. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] on these charts. The same node makes the finite-type $K$-scheme $P_\eta$ Noetherian. Choose its finite cover by Noetherian affine opens; [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] makes each chart topologically Noetherian, and a descending chain of closed sets stabilizes on the whole scheme once it stabilizes on these finitely many charts. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every open subset of $P_\eta$ is quasi-compact. In particular $a^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $V\subset Y$, so $a$ is quasi-compact. Now [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] identifies $|\Gamma|$ with the closure of $a(P_\eta)$. Continuity and the density of $\xi$ show that $y=a(\xi)$ is a generic point of $\Gamma$, lying over $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image; Noetherian affine-chart assembly written explicitly.

proof.text: Fix $x\in P$ and two points $z_1,z_2\in\pi^{-1}(x)$; write $s$ for the image of $x$ in $S$. For each $z_i\ne y$, the specialization $y\leadsto z_i$ in the locally Noetherian $\Gamma$ is traced by $b_i:\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to\Gamma$ from [lem-sbc-noetherian-specialization-trait], with $R_i$ a DVR, generic image $y$ and closed image $z_i$. If $z_i=y$, instead take $R_i=\kappa(y)$ and its canonical point map. Thus in both cases the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ maps to $\eta$ in $S$, and the closed point maps to $s$. Pull back $P,Q$ to these bases. Smoothness is preserved by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Finite presentation is preserved on affine charts by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1); quasi-compactness is part of the finite affine presentation and its base changes. The closed diagonal remains closed by its quotient-algebra description [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the group identities and the semiabelian geometric-fibre condition persist by their definitions. Hence [lem-sfb-semiabelian-trait-hom-extension] gives a group homomorphism $v_i:P_{R_i}\to Q_{R_i}$ extending $u_{L_i}$ when $R_i$ is a DVR. In the field case $v_i$ is simply the base change of $u$.

source.place: Chapter II section 2 Lemma 1 proof, valuation-ring reduction; trait selection is Stacks Tag 054F, properties.tex lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr.

proof.text: Let $p_i:\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to P$ and $q_i:\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to Q$ be the two coordinates of $b_i$. The second coordinate $v_i(p_i)$ agrees with $q_i$ on $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$: both are $u(p_i)$, since $y$ is the image of the generic point of the prescribed generic graph. They agree on the whole $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. In fact their equalizer is cut out by the pullback of the closed diagonal of $Q/S$; its ideal $I\subset R_i$ becomes zero in $L_i$. Since $R_i\hookrightarrow L_i$ is injective, $I=0$. The field case is the same argument with $R_i=L_i$. Thus $q_i$ on the closed fibre is the evaluation of $(v_i)_{k_i}$ at the point furnished by $p_i$, where $k_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$.

source.place: Elementary closed-equalizer ideal calculation; compare Tag 01RH, lemma-equality-of-morphisms.

proof.text: The closed point maps induce compatible embeddings $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\kappa(z_i)\hookrightarrow k_i$. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] over $\kappa(x)$ to embed $k_1,k_2$ into a common field $M$, then choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/M$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. In particular the two resulting maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ from $p_i$ are the same canonical point $x$ with the same embedding of $\kappa(x)$. The given extensions $v_1,v_2$ satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-semiabelian-trait-specialization-agreement]: their generic restrictions are the pullbacks of the fixed $u$, their closed base point is $s$, and the chosen embeddings $k_i\hookrightarrow\Omega$ agree on $\kappa(s)$. Thus $(v_1)_\Omega=(v_2)_\Omega$. Evaluating at that common $P$-point and using step 4 proves that the two maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Q$ from $q_i$ agree.

source.place: Chapter II section 2 Lemma 1 proof, omitted compatibility in the valuation-ring argument, made explicit by the cited comparison input.

proof.text: The two maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P\times_SQ$ just obtained have equal first and second coordinates, hence are equal by the defining universal property of the fibre product. Their images are respectively the images of $z_1,z_2$ under the closed immersion $\Gamma\hookrightarrow P\times_SQ$. This immersion is injective on underlying points by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $z_1=z_2$. Therefore $\pi^{-1}(x)$ has at most one point. The homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the underlying set of $\Gamma_x$ with this set. An empty set or a singleton is finite, proving the requested assertion. No claim about nilpotents in the fibre has been made.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q08-e7d82ea8c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item's statement is unchanged (byte-identical to live, which is still unsplit). The live item has no proof and no re-split note. The six steps are correct. Step 1: power-integrality with n=1 (the abelian variety supplies the required proper, smooth, geometrically connected quotient), then the algebraically-closed connectedness criterion, then generic-geometry-core make P_eta integral. Step 2: a is quasi-compact through Noetherian ascent and Noetherian space, and the quasi-compact clause of lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc makes y=a(xi) the generic point of Gamma. Step 3: the specialization trait is used only when z_i≠y, with kappa(y) as the field case; smoothness and finite presentation are kept under base change. Step 4: q_i=u(p_i) generically because kappa(y)=kappa(xi), and the closed-equalizer argument on the domain R_i extends this to all of Spec R_i. Step 5: the residue fields are joined over kappa(x) in one algebraically closed field, so the hypotheses of the agreement node hold, including the mixed field/DVR case with s=eta. Step 6: the fibre-product property and injectivity of the closed immersion give at most one point. trait-hom-extension is the DVR case of Faltings Lemma 1 / Faltings–Chai I.2.7, so it is true. It was checked on G_m and on a Tate-curve identity component. It is a legitimate base case: citing the parent would create a cycle. The agreement node is true, since it follows from Faltings plus uniqueness over a DVR, and the report gives an independent prime-to-p torsion / strict-henselization argument. It is not a restatement of the item: it has no graph and no fibre claim. Both new nodes are statement-only and self-contained. No duplicates were found in the snapshot or live. Batch-5: lem-trf-smooth-composition is a generic Mathlib leaf (composition of smooth morphisms) outside both assumptions, so it is accepted. The tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA citation. Faltings has no local copy (WANTED), so I checked the statements mathematically instead.
